correctness.rationale: From the downset formula for implication, a failure requires a principal downset containing both a point u in I\J and a point v in J\I; these points must be incomparable and have a common upper bound. Symmetry and the valid diagonal force failures to occur in pairs of orientations. Fix witnesses to the unique unordered failure. The separating ideals containing u but not v form exactly the interval [down(u), P\up(v)], and the reversed interval is [down(v), P\up(u)]. Every cross pair fails, so both intervals must be singletons. Thus every point other than u and v is strictly below both or strictly above both, by intersecting the two resulting partitions. Any incomparable lower points would give another failing pair of principal ideals with upper bound u. Any incomparable upper points sharing an upper bound would give another pair of principal ideals, now containing both u and v. The upper part is nonempty by the original witness and is a forest in the stated downset convention. Conversely, all comparable pairs pass; differences of two upper-type ideals lie wholly in the forest and cannot witness failure. The sole exceptional unordered pair consists of the two ideals containing exactly one of u and v. The ideal counts are k proper lower-chain ideals, three middle ideals, and |J(F)| upper-type ideals. With m=|F|>=1, k+2^m<2^(m+k) for k>=1 since 2^m(2^k-1)>k; for k=0 equality requires every subset of F to be an ideal, so F is the antichain. This proves the normalized degree and the unique equality case for every n>=3 without extrapolating the frozen finite enumeration.
residual_risks: This comparison holds within the exact two-ordered-failure class, not as a maximum over all nonprelinear algebras or for other valuation measures.

value.rationale: A standard theorem identifies the zero-failure boundary of a central Heyting identity. This result resolves its first positive boundary for arbitrary finite algebras: one local witness forces a single branching pair with a chain below it and a forest above it. The general rigidity adds information not conveyed by the previously counted extremizer, and it explains precisely where the upper size bound can be attained.
residual_risks: No inference for larger defect counts, infinite algebras or a different binary identity is established.
